title: 'A "# nolint" in a roxygen description becomes a heading'

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
#' Build the recipes table
#'
#' Aggregates the input parameters into a temporary table.
#' # nolint
#' @export
build_recipes <- function(params) {
  # ...
}
```

```text
> roxygen2::roxygenise()
Warning message:
[fct_database.R:59] @description markdown failed to process
Caused by error in `attributes(.Data) <- c(attributes(.Data), attrib)`:
! 'names' attribute [2] must be the same length as the vector [1]
```
:::

This pitfall depends on generating a package's documentation, so it cannot be replayed in the browser. The output above is the one observed in 2023.

## Why

With markdown enabled in roxygen, a line that starts with `#` followed by a space is a level 1 heading. `# nolint`, meant for {lintr}, therefore becomes a heading in the middle of the description. In 2023, {roxygen2} failed to process that markdown, with a message that said nothing about the `# nolint`: three hours of debugging in the original incident.

With {roxygen2} 8.1.0, there is no error any more, but the `.Rd` file contains an empty section named "nolint".

## The fix

Drop the space after the hash, since `#nolint` is not a markdown heading, or put the {lintr} exclusion on the line of code concerned rather than in the documentation.

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
#' Build the recipes table
#'
#' Aggregates the input parameters into a temporary table.
#' #nolint
#' @export
build_recipes <- function(params) {
  # ...
}
```
:::
